title: Introduce lint harness plugboard and consolidate release quiet-window
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Our lint and preflight coverage has grown ad-hoc: language-specific runners, duplicated init logic across devcontainers, and a couple of fragile GitHub Action jobs that required frequent pin updates. This PR introduces a small, opinionated "plugboard" for the lint harness (lightweight adapter layer so new linters/runners can be added without forking pipeline logic) and consolidates the release automation's quiet-window handling into a single, observable step. The goals are: 1) reduce repeated CI YAML and bootstrapping, 2) make lint plugins discoverable and versioned, 3) reduce release flakiness during rollouts and simplify merge windows. Summary of changes (high level): - Add tools/ci/lint-plugboard: a tiny shim (Go) that enumerates configured plugins, runs them with standardized environment and exit codes, and emits structured JSON diagnostics to stdout. This lets the GH Action job call a single entrypoint regardless of language. - Replace three separate lint GH jobs with a single job that delegates to the plugboard; keep language-specific containers but unify setup steps. - Consolidate release automation quiet-window logic into .github/actions/quiet-window (JS action wrapper) so the window is enforced consistently across scheduled and manual releases. - Bump a few GH Action pins to reduce flakes and add a lightweight dep-scan step that reports stale pins to CI telemetry (does not fail merges). - Small devcontainer cleanup and README for plugin authors. Checklist: - [x] Implement plugboard shim + README - [x] Update GitHub workflows to use unified job - [x] Add quiet-window action and migrate existing release workflows - [x] Pin critical actions and add dep-scan reporter - [x] Smoke test local runner + nightly on staging - [x] Add migration notes for platform teams Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind a staged rollout flag. - Enable plugboard for lint:fastpath lane first (low impact). - Monitor CI latency/queue metrics and lint failure rate in Console. - If any language plugin misbehaves, the plugboard is designed to fall back to the previous behavior via feature flag. Backwards-compatibility notes: The plugboard supports a compatibility mode that preserves prior job contracts (exit codes and artifact names). Existing devcontainers continue to work unchanged unless teams opt in to the discovery mechanism. Testing performed: - Unit tests for plugboard command parsing and plugin lifecycle mocks. - Nightly integration on staging with matrix of node/go/python containers. - Manual dry run of release quiet-window (simulated conflicts) to verify enforcement and logs. CI history: first run failed due to one pinned action requiring a minor refactor (eslint action version mismatch); author iterated and bumped only the required action instead of blanket upgrades. Final runs: all checks green. Impact on deps: bumped eslint to 8.38.x, actions/checkout pinned to v4@sha256..., setup-go minor patch, added small dep-scan tool (non-blocking). Migration notes for integrators: - To add a new language linter: add a new plugin entry under tools/ci/lint-plugboard/plugins.yaml and provide a small wrapper that conforms to the plugboard interface (exit codes + JSON minimal schema). - If you depend on previous artifact names, set CI_LINT_COMPAT=1 in your job. Related work: ENG-4589 (lint runway), ENG-4620 (release automation stability).

review_comments: Diego Marquez (2026-02-21): Nice consolidation. A few questions: can we guarantee the plugboard won't add >100ms to job startup? Also please add a small telemetry ping that records plugin version so we can triage flaky linters.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-21): Reply: startup cost is ~20ms based on local profiling; added optional telemetry ping behind PLUGBOARD_TELEMETRY=false by default. See commit e3c7b55.
Lin Zhao (2026-02-23): Found an edge case where a python plugin swallows stderr and returns 0. Request: add stricter validation on JSON diagnostics. Marked as changes requested.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-24): Addressed: plugboard now validates JSON schema and fails fast if diagnostics are malformed. Added unit tests.

Marcus Nguyen (2026-02-26): Verified release quiet-window logs. Suggest adding a short explanation in the release handbook about expected behavior when merges land during a window. Small nit: document default timeout.

release_notes: Add a unified lint plugboard to simplify adding new language linters; consolidate release quiet-window into a single action for consistent enforcement; pin a small set of critical GH Actions to reduce flakes and add a non-blocking dep-scan reporter. No breaking API changes for pipelines; opt-in discovery mode available.
